ops.title: Snapshot IO fix 1: batch predicate work per graph request (blocked on the owner's batching choice)
ops.description:
Not implemented. The snapshot IO work of 2026-10-10 shipped the duplicate-validation removal, prepared-cache read accounting, warm pacing, and the 512 MiB fact budget (cc-transcript 14.40.0, capt-hook 12.92.8). Batching predicate work so one graph request reads each fact once across its predicates was left out because the owner has not chosen a batching design, and the instruction was not to pick a default.

What is recorded about the choice: the options were put to the owner and none was selected. A refuter pass set obligations any design must meet: option A must be ordered and primary-driven; option C's reuse must reject a changed source or context; and an exact regression test must pin the any-of correctness case. Mandatory-hook grouping and eager evaluation across unrelated hooks are out of scope by ruling.

Until then, a request with several predicates can read the same prepared fact more than once. `prepared_cache_reads` and `prepared_cache_bytes_read` in `usage` now make that visible per request.

ops.text: The owner has chosen a batching design; no default was picked by an agent
A graph request with several predicates reads each prepared fact at most once, shown by prepared_cache_reads in usage
Option A, if chosen, is ordered and primary-driven; option C reuse, if chosen, rejects a changed source or context
An exact regression test pins the any-of correctness case
